patients.summary: Thirty-year-old administrative assistant who joins in July 2024 with right carpal tunnel syndrome, treated with a night splint. Her second pregnancy (2025-2026) is complicated by mild gestational hypertension at 35 weeks and ends in a precipitous term vaginal delivery after an ED presentation; the hypertension resolves postpartum.

events.reason: New patient; numbness and tingling right hand

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 30 y/o F, admin assistant. Moving her care here; prior PCP and OB were at a group out of the area. Records release signed today.

CC: R hand numbness/tingling.

HPI: Started roughly six weeks ago. Thumb, index and middle finger on the right, pinky spared. Much worse at night; a couple of nights a week it wakes her up and she shakes the hand out. Notices it some days at the keyboard too. No injury, no fall on the hand, never had this before. No neck pain. Left hand fine.

PMH: nothing chronic. G1P1 - term vaginal delivery 2021, uncomplicated per pt.
PSH: none.
Meds: prenatal vitamin daily (she and her husband would like a second child in the next year or so and her OB had her start it).
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother had preeclampsia with one of her pregnancies and a very fast labor with another.
SH: admin assistant, mostly computer work. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: well appearing. Neck full ROM, Spurling negative. R wrist: no swelling, no redness or warmth. Tinel's positive at the R carpal tunnel. Phalen's brings on her tingling at about 30 sec. Thenar bulk normal. Grip and APB strength 5/5 bilaterally. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis. Sensation otherwise intact. L wrist Tinel/Phalen negative. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P:
1. R carpal tunnel syndrome - classic hx and exam, no weakness or atrophy. Neutral-position wrist splint at night, try to keep the wrist straight at the keyboard (she's going to ask about a keyboard tray and wrist rest at work). Video f/u in about 2 months; if not better or any weakness, will talk about next steps.
2. Health maintenance - baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH today; HIV and hep C screen offered and she accepts. Pap with HPV per prior records - will confirm when records come. PHQ-2 0.
3. Preconception - continue prenatal vitamin.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records request faxed to prior primary care and OB group with signed release. Requested last 5 years of office notes, labs, immunizations, Pap results and delivery summary.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Monica - all of your bloodwork from Monday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid and cholesterol. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Let me know how the splint is going.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Prior Practice Records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records received from prior primary care/OB group (48 pages), scanned to chart. Includes office notes 2019-2024, immunization record, Pap/HPV 09/2022, and labor and delivery summary from 2021. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed prior records. G1P1, SVD at term in 2021, uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery, normotensive throughout. Tdap given in that pregnancy (03/2021). COVID primary series 2021. Pap with HPV 09/2022 negative/negative - next due 2027. No chronic problems or meds other than prenatal vitamin. Immunization list updated.

documents.title: Splint question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, quick question. The splint is helping at night, I'm sleeping through most nights now. Should I be wearing it at work too? It makes typing kind of awkward. Thanks, Monica

documents.title: RE: Splint question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad it's helping. Nights are the important part. During the day you don't need to wear it while typing - focus on keeping the wrist flat and taking short breaks. If you have a flare during the day, wearing it for a while is fine. We'll check in at the video visit in September.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - Carpal Tunnel Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from her office, ID confirmed.

R CTS f/u. Wearing the splint nightly since July. Now only woken by it rarely, maybe once in a few weeks. Daytime tingling here and there on long typing days, settles when she shakes it out or takes a break. Work got her a keyboard tray. No weakness, not dropping things.

Obs on video: no distress, opposes thumb to each finger without difficulty, makes full fist.

A/P: R carpal tunnel syndrome, improving with conservative care. Keep the night splint, keep the ergonomic changes. Let me know if numbness becomes constant or any weakness. Flu shot this fall - nurse visit booked.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu and updated COVID vaccines. Not pregnant per pt. Screening questions negative, VIS provided. Flu 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, COVID 0.3 mL IM R deltoid. Lots recorded. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Rescheduled from earlier this month (childcare).

Interval: doing well. R wrist - rarely bothers her now; she puts the splint on a night or two when it acts up after a heavy stretch at work. No daytime numbness, no weakness. She and her husband are planning to try for a second baby this fall/winter. Still on the prenatal vitamin.

ROS otherwise negative. PHQ-9 2.

Meds: prenatal vitamin. NKDA. FH unchanged (mother - preeclampsia, rapid labor). Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: well, pleasant. HEENT normal, no thyroid enlargement or nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. R wrist: Tinel's and Phalen's negative today, thenar bulk and strength normal. Skin no concerning lesions. No edema.

A/P:
1. Preventive - Pap/HPV 2022 negative, next 2027. Labs from last summer normal; no repeat needed. Flu shot in the fall. Tdap will be due in the next pregnancy.
2. R carpal tunnel - quiet, splint as needed.
3. Preconception - continue prenatal vitamin. Mentioned her mother's history of preeclampsia is worth telling her OB at the first prenatal visit. Call us with a positive test and we'll get her to OB.

RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Screening negative, VIS given, lot recorded. Tolerated well. Declined COVID booster today, may get it later.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, straightforward MDM

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning! I got a positive home test today. My last period started October 17. Do I come in or go straight to an OB? My last one was too far away now, so happy to go wherever you recommend.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Pregnancy Test
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in on lunch break after portal message. LMP 10/17/25, regular cycles, about 4 weeks 6 days by dates. Urine hCG positive in office. Feels well, no bleeding or cramping. Taking prenatal vitamin daily. Reviewed with PCP: referral placed to OB, pt aware OB office will call to schedule a new OB visit at around 8 weeks. Reminded to avoid alcohol and to call with bleeding or severe pain.
